acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Configure Review→Approved to set an internal reviewed flag and reviewer identifier. Verify declared values, stable actor identity and before/after history. Reject an unknown field, invalid type or unauthorized protected-field update without partially changing state. Fail a later synchronous task: verify the transactional update and state rollback together. Retry the same event and re-enter the state through an allowed path: follow an explicit overwrite/re-entry policy without duplicating history or side effects. Never replace an approved signed document silently.

Save a draft workflow without activating it; verify the effective active configuration remains unchanged. Activate it explicitly, then test both a newly created matter/document and one created before activation. Record which workflow revision each follows; do not assume the tutorial proves migration of existing pending records.

The normal-case example is insufficient acceptance evidence. Add rejection, return-for-correction, cancellation and stale-record attempts. Verify lifecycle status separately from approval labels. A rejected orfailed record must not be treated as submitted orready to file.

Disable email alerts, advance to approval, and verify that no notification wasqueued orsent. Keep the approval task independently visible. Re-enable alerts and test actual recipient, content, delivery failure and retry evidence. Never treat narration about an email as proof of sending orreceipt.

Create two users with the approver role and one user with only state-specific edit rights. Verify editing and transitioning are distinct permissions. Do not interpret a role grant as a unique person. Attempt all transitions as each user, then revoke a role and test immediate access including direct API endpoints.
